title: 003 — GitHub Copilot code review via API, and four Copilot models retired
html:
003 — GitHub Copilot code review via API, and four Copilot models retired

The one idea: Copilot code review can now be requested from the GitHub REST and GraphQL APIs, so a pipeline or bot can ask for an AI review without a person clicking a button. In the same week GitHub retired four Copilot models, which matters if your team or your automation pinned one of them.

Added 2026-10-06 · Released 2026-10-02 by GitHub

1. What it is

Two GitHub Copilot changes landed on 2 October 2026:

  • Code review through the API. You can request a Copilot code review with the REST or GraphQL API. The changelog says the effort level can be set per request. The default effort is now named Balanced (it was "Default"), and Lite is the other option. The new default name applies from 28 September 2026.
  • Model retirements. Four models were deprecated across all Copilot experiences:
Retired model Suggested replacement
Gemini 3.5 Flash Gemini 3.8 Flash
Gemini 3.6 Flash Gemini 3.8 Flash
Kimi K2.7 Code Kimi K3
Claude Opus 4.7 Claude Opus 5.5

Code review is available on Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business and Enterprise.

2. Why it matters

  • Review becomes a pipeline step. Until now an AI review was mostly requested by hand or by a repository rule. With API access, a release bot, a merge-queue job or an internal tool can ask for a review at the moment it makes sense, for example only on PRs that touch a risky folder.
  • Cost and depth are now a choice per request. Lite for small, low-risk changes and Balanced for the rest lets a team spend premium usage where the risk is.
  • Model pinning breaks quietly. Teams that standardised on a model (in an agent config, a prompt library or an org policy) need to move to the replacement. Enterprise admins may have to enable the replacement models in policy before people can pick them.

3. How it works

---
title: Copilot code review requested by automation
---
flowchart LR
    P["PR opened or updated"] --> J["CI job or bot"]
    J --> D{"Touches risky paths?"}
    D -- yes --> B["Request review<br/>(Balanced)"]
    D -- no --> L["Request review<br/>(Lite) or skip"]
    B --> R["Copilot posts review comments"]
    L --> R
    R --> H["Human reviewer decides"]

Copilot reviews like any other reviewer: it leaves comments on the PR. It does not approve or block a merge, so branch protection and human review still apply.

Effort settings are layered. Enterprise, organization, repository and personal settings exist, and the lower level overrides the higher one.

4. How to use it

GitHub's docs say a review can be requested through the REST API by adding copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot] as a reviewer, using the standard "request reviewers" endpoint:

curl -L -X POST \
  -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN" \
  https://api.github.com/repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/PULL_NUMBER/requested_reviewers \
  -d '{"reviewers":["copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]"]}'

The same call from C#:

using System.Net.Http.Json;

using var http = new HttpClient { BaseAddress = new Uri("https://api.github.com/") };
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.UserAgent.ParseAdd("review-bot");
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Accept.ParseAdd("application/vnd.github+json");
http.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization =
    new("Bearer", Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("GITHUB_TOKEN"));

var body = new { reviewers = new[] { "copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]" } };
using var response = await http.PostAsJsonAsync(
    $"repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pullNumber}/requested_reviewers", body);
response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode();

The changelog says effort can be chosen per API request, but the pages read for this note do not show the parameter name. Check the code review docs before relying on it, and set the default in repository or organization settings meanwhile.

For the model retirements: search your repos and agent configs for the retired model names, switch to the replacements, and (as an admin) confirm the replacements are enabled under the Copilot model policies.

5. Trade-offs and limits

  • Not a gate. Treat Copilot's comments as a first pass. Required reviews by people stay in place.
  • Usage cost. Automated requests on every push add up. Trigger reviews on meaningful events (ready for review, risky paths) rather than every commit.
  • Plan dependent. Free plans are not in the availability list.
  • Model churn. Model names in Copilot change every few months. Keep model choices in one config file, not scattered through scripts.

6. Where it fits

  • AI in the SDLC: where AI review fits next to human review.
  • Testing and quality: review as one quality gate among several.
  • Infrastructure and platform: CI pipelines that would call the API.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why is it safer to request Copilot review only on selected PRs rather than on every push?
  2. What does Copilot review not do that a required human review does?
  3. Your team's agent config pins Claude Opus 4.7. What breaks, and what are the steps to fix it?
  4. Effort can be set at enterprise, organization, repository and personal level. Which one wins?

Sources

  • Selected models in GitHub Copilot deprecated — GitHub Changelog, 2 Oct 2026
